articles.title: Ty Lue Dedicates Clippers' Win in NBA Opener to Steve Ballmer, 'Still Fighting for Him'
articles.summary: Los Angeles Clippers head coach Ty Lue dedicated Wednesday's season-opening, 121-96 win over the Sacramento Kings to team governor Steve Ballmer.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Clippers head coach Ty Lue dedicated Wednesday's season-opening, 121-96 win over the Sacramento Kings to team governor Steve Ballmer.

Speaking to reporters after the convincing victory, Lue told reporters , "First off, that win was for Mr. Ballmer. Just want to say thank you for everything and we're still fighting for him."

Lue went on to add, "We keep him in our hearts. He provided a great living for everyone in this arena. One of the best men that I know."

Ballmer is serving a one-year suspension handed down by the NBA for his role in salary cap circumvention related to former Clippers star Kawhi Leonard's $28 million endorsement deal with Aspiration Fund Adviser LLC.

In addition to the Clippers being docked $30 million and five future first-round draft picks, Ballmer is not permitted to participate in any league or team activities for an entire year.

After trading Leonard to the Toronto Raptors during the offseason and amid all of the drama related to his situation, there were major question marks regarding how the Clippers would fare in 2026-27.

Although it was only one game, early returns were excellent, as L.A. cruised to an impressive home win over Sacramento.

Guard Darius Garland was the leading performer by far, leading all players with 30 points on 11-of-19 shooting from the field to go along with four assists.

Garland echoed Lue's sentiments regarding Ballmer, saying, "He was definitely here in spirit. Somebody was at his seats and we felt the energy. It wasn't his energy, but we felt his energy."

Entering this season, Lue led the Clippers to the playoffs in four of his six seasons at the helm, and the team has never finished .500 or worse with him as head coach.

They narrowly missed the playoffs last season with a 42-40 record, but Wednesday's showing suggests they have a chance to bounce back and return to the postseason mix.

Lue and the Clippers will look to keep rolling Friday when they face the rival Los Angeles Lakers at the Lakers' Crypto.com Arena.

articles.title: Anthony Davis Drops Honest Quote About Wizards Crowd in Video After Win in NBA Opener vs. Bucks
articles.summary: Anthony Davis' debut with the Washington Wizards was a successful one with a 128-116 win over the Milwaukee Bucks, but one thing he took notice of was the home crowd at Capital One Arena.
articles.body:
Anthony Davis' debut with the Washington Wizards was a successful one with a 128-116 win over the Milwaukee Bucks, but one thing he took notice of was the home crowd at Capital One Arena.

Davis praised the fans who were in attendance, but told reporters he would have liked to see it be "a little more packed" and joked there were times last season when it looked like "'Dress Like a Seat Night' in here."

Warriors, Heat, on Wrong Side of History 😬

Monumental Sports, which owns the Wizards, notes Capital One Arena can hold 20,000 fans for the various pro sports teams in the Washington D.C. area.

The listed attendance for Wednesday's season-opening game between the Bucks and Wizards was 18,805, according to Basketball Reference . It's the ninth-biggest crowd among the 14 teams that have played a home game so far.

One reason the Wizards might have fallen short of a sellout was the absence of No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa. He suffered an ankle sprain in the preseason finale on Oct. 16 that kept him out of the season opener.

But this is still a Wizards team with good star power, like Davis and Trae Young, that it's a bit of a surprise there were some empty seats for the first game.

Another thing that probably didn't help was that the Bucks, after trading Giannis Antetokounmpo in the offseason, were the opponent.

It can also take time for a franchise that has struggled like the Wizards have for an extended period to win back fan enthusiasm. They haven't finished with a winning record since the 2017-18 season and went 50-196 over the past three seasons combined.

Wednesday was an encouraging sign for what this Wizards team, led by Davis and Young, can become as long as they stay healthy.

Davis put up 34 points and 12 rebounds in his first game since Jan. 8 when he was still with the Dallas Mavericks. Young had 20 points and 13 assists in 38 minutes.

When Dybantsa eventually gets added into the mix, the Wizards will look a lot more interesting than they have in a long time.

articles.title: Yaxel Lendeborg says he 'lost all respect' for Luka Dončić in first NBA game: 'I was telling him he sucks'
articles.summary: Luka Dončić dropped a game-high 28 points in the Lakers' win.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg was given a tough task in his first NBA game. In his NBA debut, Lendeborg was tasked with stopping Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Dončić, one of the most explosive scorers in the league.

Some rookies might shy away from that assignment, knowing Dončić has the ability to make even veteran defenders look mediocre. Lendeborg, apparently, isn't most rookies.

The Warriors forward went right at Dončić, engaging in some tense trash talk throughout the contest. Lendeborg didn't back down after the game — a 127-105 win by the Lakers — either, saying he told Dončić "he sucks."

Lendeborg added that he "lost all respect" for Dončić after seeing the way the Lakers star plays the game up close. Lendeborg specifically called out Dončić's "complaining" throughout the game.

Lendeborg did take things a bit too far with his trash talk, however. In his first NBA game, the rookie was given a technical foul before halftime.

Dončić didn't seem too bothered by Lendeborg's trash talk. The Lakers star finished the contest with a team-leading 28 points … and led the Lakers to a win.

After the game, Dončić said he elevated his play due to Lendeborg's antics.

Dončić later added that Lendeborg was " talking crazy " the entire night.

Despite Dončić's numbers and the Lakers' win, it seems unlikely Lendeborg will change his approach any time soon. The rookie had the support of Draymond Green after the game, with Green using some colorful language to encourage Lendeborg to keep talking trash, regardless of his opponent.

articles.title: Damian Lillard Talks Return From Injury, Blazers Reunion After Blowout Win vs. Suns
articles.summary: After 18 months away from the court, Portland Trail Blazers star guard Damian Lillard made his triumphant return in Wednesday's 124-83 blowout win over the Phoenix Suns.
articles.body:
After 18 months away from the court, Portland Trail Blazers star guard Damian Lillard made his triumphant return in Wednesday's 124-83 blowout win over the Phoenix Suns.

Lillard dropped a game-high 25 points with six three-pointers to spearhead the victory, showing that he's back to his old self after spending a year and a half recovering from a torn Achilles suffered in April 2025 when he was with the Milwaukee Bucks.

"I did feel good, but you know I've felt good for months now, and I've been saying that. But I think there's probably some people that might have been skeptical because they hadn't seen me. I hadn't been out on the floor and been in front of people," Lillard said after the game, per the Associated Press .

Lillard began his NBA career in Portland in 2012 before his brief two-year stint in Milwaukee, and he returned to his longtime franchise on a three-year, $42 million deal in July 2025. Despite missing the entire 2025-26 season, he received a warm welcome from fans at Moda Center with an extended standing ovation before his pregame address.

"It was a lot of love. The fans showed a lot of love," Lillard said. "I think it's no secret the relationship between myself and our fans and the city of Portland."

If Lillard can stay healthy throughout the year, the Blazers should be able to keep up with the top teams in the Western Conference.

"Coming back off of a major injury, getting back healthy, and making it to this day, being a part of a really good team -- at a different time for the Trail Blazers than my last stint with the team -- it just felt great to be embraced and welcomed," Lillard said.

articles.title: Maryland Unveils Throwback Uniforms Honoring 2002 MCBB Title Team in Hype Video, Photos
articles.summary: Maryland is celebrating the 25th anniversary season of the 2001-02 men's basketball championship team in style.
articles.body:
Maryland is celebrating the 25th anniversary season of the 2001-02 men's basketball championship team in style.

The Terrapins unveiled their new championship throwback uniforms that will be used during the 2026-27 season as they honor one of the great teams in the history of the program.

Maryland will wear the uniforms for three games during the upcoming season, including the opener against Bucknell on Nov. 2, against Illinois on Jan. 16 and against Indiana on Feb. 13.

Specific details in the throwback uniform include the arch Maryland across the chest; the Maryland "M" flag and red stripe on the right leg of the shorts; and the black, red and gold trim around the neckline and arms.

The matchup with IU at Xfinity Center will include a celebration of the 2002 national championship team.

Indiana was the team Maryland defeated in that title game, 64-52, to win what remains the only championship for the men's basketball program.

The 2001-02 Maryland squad still holds the program's single-season wins record. They finished 32-4 overall and went 15-1 in ACC play to earn a No. 1 seed in the NCAA tournament.

Maryland won each of its six tournament games by at least eight points, with four wins by double-digits. Juan Dixon was named Most Outstanding Player of the tournament after averaging 25.8 points on 54.2 percent shooting.

Dixon, Steve Blake and Lonny Baxter were all part of the 2001-02 team who have subsequently had their jerseys hung from the rafters at Xfinity Center.

Gary Williams, who was Maryland's head coach from 1989 to 2011, was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame and College Basketball Hall of Fame in 2014.

articles.title: 1 Overreaction to Every NBA Team's First Game
articles.summary: Welcome back, NBA. We missed you more than you know.
articles.body:
Welcome back, NBA. We missed you more than you know.

The 2026-27 season is officially underway, with everyone outside of the Cleveland Cavaliers and Denver Nuggets playing their first game by Wednesday night.

We've already seen Paul George score a Boston Celtics franchise record for a team debut with 38 points, Victor Wembanyama struggle mightily against the San Antonio Spurs' biggest rivals and LeBron James enjoying a "home" victory at Madison Square Garden with his new Philadelphia 76ers teammates.

Did the Celtics actually win the Jaylen Brown trade? Has the league figured out how to stop Wemby? Are the 76ers the newest superteam who should be considered the title favorites? It's time to overreact to every NBA team's first game of the 2026-27 season.

ATL | BKN | BOS | CHA | CHI | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GSW | HOU | IND | LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN | NOP | NYK | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX | POR | SAC | SAS | TOR | UTA | WAS

A big 132-125 road win over the Orlando Magic has the Atlanta Hawks making sure no one forgets about them when talking about the elite teams in the East.

This was a franchise that took off following the Trae Young trade last year and now is deeper than ever with the additions of Lu Dort and Aaron Wiggins.

Atlanta boasts a balanced scoring attack—four players scored between 19 and 31 points against Orlando—and impressive depth. The Hawks used a nine-man rotation but have other reliable options, both veterans and young players, on the bench.

The Hawks are going to be really good this year, even in an improved East. Knocking off another potential playoff team in the Magic helps prove this will be a top-6 seed.

Boston Celtics: The Jaylen Brown-Paul George Trade Doesn't Look That Bad

The Jaylen Brown-Paul George trade shocked the NBA world this past summer and ultimately could have made the difference between LeBron James signing with the Philadelphia 76ers or elsewhere.

While Brown had a solid debut for Philly (19 points on 7-of-14 shooting, eight rebounds, six assists in 35 minutes) it was the 36-year-old George who stole the show.

On arguably the worst contract in the NBA ( $54.1 million ) given his age and lack of durability, George scored a franchise-record 38 points in his Boston Celtics debut.

Maybe this trade wasn't as terrible as we all assumed it to be at the time?

It's going to be a long, weird, disappointing season for Brooklyn Nets fans, as the team doesn't have the talent to win yet doesn't own the right to keep its 2027 first-round pick .

The Nets lost at home to a Charlotte Hornets squad that had to start a backcourt of Dennis Schröder and Sion James with Coby White and Kon Knueppel sidelined due to injury. Even with Julius Randle now in the starting lineup, the Nets mustered just 103 total points with Randle and Michael Porter Jr. the only two players to crack double digits in scoring.

Brooklyn left much of its collection of former first-round picks on the bench or out of the rotation altogether, not a great sign for any sort of talent development this season.

The Nets could be the worst team in basketball and opening night only helped confirm these fears.

Final Record Predictions for Every NBA Team 🔮

Charlotte Hornets: Brandon Miller Will Struggle Without LaMelo Ball

After trading LaMelo Ball, Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel have taken over as the faces of the Charlotte Hornets. The franchise just handed Miller a five-year, $209 million extension to help reward him for a season where he averaged 20.2 points on 38.3 percent shooting from deep.

How much did Ball factor into Miller's success, however?

In his first game without Ball on the Hornets, Miller shot just 3-of-14 from three and 7-of-21 overall for his 18 points while recording only a single assist. This comes a year after Miller made 56.1 percent of his twos and a healthy 40.3 percent of his threes off passes from Ball, per the NBA's tracking data .

Miller will have to prove he's worth $40-plus million a year, especially without an elite table setter beside him.

Chicago Bulls: Still Not Close to Playoff Contention

The Chicago Bulls are headed in the right direction, really! It's just going to take some more time.

Norman Powell was a smart signing. Caleb Wilson is going to be a star. Nic Claxton is going to improve the team's defense. As a 135-92 opening night loss to the Toronto Raptors taught us, however, Chicago just isn't going to be able to hang with the best in the East this season.

Wilson went just 7-of-21 from the field and 1-of-8 from three in his NBA debut, Josh Giddey was a minus-39 while scoring just two points and the Raptors got whatever they wanted on the offensive end.

This year will be about development for the Bulls, while fielding trade calls for Powell before the deadline.

Dallas Mavericks: Kyrie Irving is Still an All-Star Talent

Kyrie Irving is exactly what the Dallas Mavericks lacked last season: a dynamic guard who can wreak havoc with his ball-handling, scoring and playmaking.

Irving returned to the court for the first time since tearing his ACL in March 2025 and looked very comfortable even at age 34.

The veteran played just 24 minutes, yet scored 15 points on 6-of-9 shooting overall. We can question whether his age lines up with this young core, although Irving's skill set will be a welcome addition alongside Cooper Flagg for now.

Detroit Pistons: No Big Trade Was Needed

The Detroit Pistons found themselves in a 3-1 hole in the first round of the East playoffs, despite being the No. 1 seed following a 60-win season.

While they eventually won the series, a second-round loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers made it seem like the Pistons would need to make a major offseason move to become true title contenders in a now loaded Eastern Conference.

The moves to swap out Tobias Harris, Caris LeVert and Isaiah Stewart for John Collins and Isaiah Joe were hardly blockbusters, but perhaps keeping the core group of guys together is actually enough?

A big opening-day win over the Boston Celtics that saw the Pistons erase a 22-point deficit reminded us how good Detroit can be. Seeing Jalen Duren (22 points, nine rebounds) ball out after such a disappointing postseason was refreshing, especially following a summer full of contract drama.

Maybe the Pistons are already title-worthy given the growth of this core.

Golden State Warriors: Stephen Curry Shouldn't Have Signed an Extension

The Golden State Warriors lost to the Los Angeles Lakers 127-105 on opening night, but in fairness to LA, it was never really this close.

The Warriors lost the second and third quarters by a combined 33 points and never had a chance, especially with Jimmy Butler, Kristaps Porziņģis, Moses Moody and Brandin Podziemski all missing the game. The first three are all on extended ( or permanent ) absences.

Stephen Curry, 38, agreed to a two-year, $116 million extension in the offseason, meaning he's under contract for the next three seasons and now can't be traded until next summer.

Legacies are cool and the money is great, but Curry isn't going to sniff the playoffs with this roster, much less another championship. It's a sad way to see one of the all-time greats go out.

Houston Rockets: Kevin Durant is Not Human

LeBron James deserves all the flowers he's been given for still playing at a high level now just two months shy of turning 42, but more attention needs to be paid to 38-year-old Kevin Durant.

Now in his 20th season, Durant dropped an easy 30 points on 10-of-16 shooting in a 128-110 win over the Dallas Mavericks, including six rebounds, three assists, a steal and a block across 37 minutes.

Already the No. 5 overall scorer in NBA history , Durant could easily pass Kobe Bryant and take his spot in the top four by the end of the season.

Durant's play at this stage of his career is nothing short of amazing.

Indiana Pacers: Tyrese Haliburton is an MVP Candidate

Tyrese Haliburton isn't going to put up the raw scoring numbers of guards like Shai Gilgeous-Alexander or Luka Dončić, although he may not have to to be in the MVP conversation this year.

Playing in his first game since the 2025 NBA Finals, Haliburton looked great coming off a torn Achilles, putting up 23 points and 12 assists in a 123-120 road win over the New Orleans Pelicans.

We saw what the Pacers looked like last year without Haliburton, and it wasn't pretty. If the 26-year-old leads Indiana to a top-3 seed in the East, he should be a frontrunner for MVP this season.

Los Angeles Clippers: Sneaky Play-in Team?

The Los Angeles Clippers have largely been written off following a tumultuous summer, and the team has already been hit by injuries to Brandon Ingram and Max Strus.

Still, Darius Garland is a two-time All-Star who dropped 30 points in a 121-96 thumping of the Sacramento Kings. If the defense on this team is legit with Derrick Jones Jr., Kris Dunn, Brook Lopez and others, head coach Ty Lue is still one of the best in the world at what he does.

The Clippers don't control their first-round pick this season and there are enough veterans on this team that winning will still be important and attainable. Maybe Los Angeles won't be as bad as we thought.

Los Angeles Lakers: Walker Kessler Was Worth the Picks

It was quite the Los Angeles Lakers debut for Walker Kessler, who scored 26 points on a perfect 12-of-12 shooting while pulling down nine rebounds, blocking two shots and finishing plus-24 in a win over the Golden State Warriors.

Obviously, playing with a passer like Luka Dončić helps.

The Lakers gave up A LOT for Kessler in the summer, as a four-year, $129.5 million contract was just the starting point. LA also sacrificed unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 as well as 2028 and 2030 first-round swaps to the Utah Jazz.

At least for one night, Kessler looked like he's worth it.

Memphis Grizzlies: Ty Jerome is NBA's Most Underrated Player

Ty Jerome tried to show us what he can do in a starting role in the second half of the season last year, as health is seemingly the only thing that can hold him back.

A cool 45 points on opening night in a 123-103 win over the Utah Jazz set a Memphis Grizzlies franchise record, as Jerome plays with a confidence few players in the NBA possess.

Jerome had arguably the best opening night of any player in the association, pairing his 45 points with seven rebounds, six assists, a block and just one turnover while going 17-of-25 from the field.

We knew he was one of the NBA's most underrated players , although he may have officially claimed his spot at the top.

A Giannis Antetokounmpo-Bam Adebayo frontcourt may be the best in the NBA, especially defensively. The guards on this Miami Heat roster, however, leave a lot to be desired.

A 36-year-old Klay Thompson is not a starter, although he may be Miami's best option at shooting guard right now. Tim Hardaway Jr. went just 1-of-7 from three in his debut and Davion Mitchell's strengths lie on the defensive end.

Can the Heat survive with average guard play at best, or will a tough East be too much to overcome with this level of weakness at the position?

Milwaukee Bucks: Jaime Jaquez Jr. Could Win Most Improved Player

Jaime Jaquez Jr. was one of the key pieces coming over from the Miami Heat in the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade. He's since won a starting job and already looks like a breakout year is coming.

Despite starting just a single game for the Heat last season, Jaquez has long been deserving of a bigger role. He and Tyler Herro looked like the only Bucks players who had any kind of offensive juice on opening night against the Washington Wizards, as Jaquez went for 22 points on 8-of-12 shooting overall while grabbing seven rebounds and passing out two assists. Jaquez was the only rotation member not to register a negative plus-minus game rating for Milwaukee.

The Bucks are going to be awful this year, although Jaquez could win the Most Improved Player award with a big season in a new starting role.

Minnesota Timberwolves: Could Challenge Thunder, Spurs as Best Team in West

Going into an emotional environment in Miami with Giannis Antetokounmpo making his Heat debut, the Minnesota Timberwolves showed no fear in a massive 131-106 win.

Anthony Edwards hit nine threes en route to his 45 points, LaMelo Ball was awesome in his Wolves debut with 21 points and six assists and there appeared to be a new energy surrounding the team overall.

The core of a great defense remains with Rudy Gobert and Jaden McDaniels. If Edwards and Ball look like the NBA's best backcourt and Jonathan Kuminga thrives in a starting power forward role, this Minnesota team could be elite.

New Orleans Pelicans: Not Far Off From Contention

The New Orleans Pelicans didn't do much this offseason, with a late-summer signing of Bennedict Mathurin their only significant move.

When healthy, however, this roster actually has a lot of talent.

Zion Williamson scored 22 points in the Pelicans' season opener, hitting two three-pointers for the first time in almost four years(!!!), going back to December 11, 2022. Dejounte Murray shined with 23 points and seven assists and seven players in total reached double figures.

Do all these pieces necessarily fit? No, although Williamson becoming a threat from outside the arc will certainly help. Let's not rule out the Pelicans as a playoff team just yet.

New York Knicks: The Honeymoon is Officially Over

The New York Knicks were the kings of summer 2026. Celebrating a title, throwing a massive parade and Jalen Brunson becoming the first active NBA player in nearly 20 years to host SNL helped cap off a magical few months for the team and its fans.

Some ugly contract negotiations cast a shadow on the end of the offseason, however, and an opening night home loss to a Philadelphia 76ers team that was newly pieced together this season officially means the honeymoon is over.

The reality is that the Knicks can't coast to a top-3 seed in the East again this season. The conference is much better and every team is going to give New York its best effort.

Given the talent in the East, the Knicks aren't even a lock to make the playoffs as a top-6 seed.

Oklahoma City Thunder: Best Team in Franchise History?

The 2024-25 Oklahoma City Thunder brought home the NBA title. The 2025-26 version won an NBA-best 64 games and reached the West Finals. This 2026-27 collection may be the best yet.

Exorcising their playoff demons by defeating the Spurs in San Antonio on opening night, the Thunder certainly look hungry, motivated and dominant on both ends of the floor.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 32 points without much free-throw help (3-of-4 from the line), Jared McCain dropped 20 points on 6-of-8 shooting from three off the bench and rookie 7'3" center Aday Mara held his ground against Victor Wembanyama.

The Thunder should be considered the title favorites, as they have the best and deepest roster in the entire league.

Orlando Magic: A Major Shakeup is Needed

There's a lot to like about this Orlando Magic team, one that's reached the playoffs the past three years.

It's also fair to question whether this core has reached its peak together.

Giving up 132 points at home to the Atlanta Hawks on opening night was a rough start, especially for a franchise that prides itself on defense. Paolo Banchero looking like an All-Star once again (35 points, 10 assists, seven rebounds) should guarantee his safety, although the rest of the roster may not feel as comfortable.

The Magic already made a change at head coach this past offseason. If this team hovers around the play-in area in the East, the next logical step is to trade a member of the core.

Philadelphia 76ers: Joel Embiid Doesn't Fit

Joel Embiid has been the biggest (literally) part of the Philadelphia 76ers for the past decade-plus. Even after just one game, it's easy to see how he may not fit with this current version, however.

Embiid led the NBA in post-up points per game last season (6.3), and moves much slower than the new-look roster around him, even with his offseason weight loss.

By comparison, Tyrese Maxey, LeBron James and Jaylen Brown all finished in the top-4 in transition points per game last year and VJ Edgecombe is a 6'4" bolt of lightning who shot 58.6 percent in fastbreak opportunities. This isn't a roster designed to slow things down and wait for Embiid to post up.

A 4-of-15 shooting performance from Embiid in the first game of the season vs. the New York Knicks isn't encouraging for his future with the team.

The Phoenix Suns were one of the biggest surprises of the 2025-26 season, only to go out and sacrifice their depth, shooting and future draft capital to acquire Miles Bridges.

Bridges was awful in his Suns debut, scoring just eight points on 3-of-11 shooting with no assists while registering a minus-35 in his 29 minutes. This roster has too many mouths to feed with Bridges, Devin Booker, Jalen Green and Dillon Brooks all in the starting lineup with no true point guard to get them the ball.

Someone is going to have to go before the end of the season (Green), as this starting five needs more playmaking, rebounding and defensive fortitude overall.

Portland Trail Blazers: Damian Lillard-Ja Morant Combo Is Going to Work

A double point guard starting backcourt of Damian Lillard and Ja Morant is certainly a wonky fit on paper, especially with durability and defensive concerns.

At least for one night, the combo looked like the second coming of Isiah Thomas and Joe Dumars.

Lillard made his return to the Portland Trail Blazers and from a torn Achilles to put up 25 points and six assists on 6-of-10 from deep while Morant added 14 points, eight assists, five rebounds, three steals and several key hustle plays that helped energize the Blazers and lead them to a 124-83 thumping of the Phoenix Suns.

The pair's individual plus-minus figures totaled plus-56, and they looked better than most of us could have imagined. Did Portland quietly pull off the trade of the summer?

Sacramento Kings: Hardest NBA Team to Watch?

The Brooklyn Nets may be the worst team in the NBA this season, although the Sacramento Kings won't be far behind.

Giving up 121 points to the Los Angeles Clippers on opening night wasn't surprising, as this could be the worst defense we've ever seen. Only scoring 96 with players like Domantas Sabonis, Zach LaVine, De'Andre Hunter, Keegan Murray and No. 7 overall pick Darius Acuff Jr. was eye-opening, however.

Acuff had a horrible pro debut, missing 19 of his 24 shots, including an 0-of-7 mark from three. The rookie had more turnovers (four) than assists (three) and was a minus-23 overall for the game. He's going to annoy his veteran teammates very quickly with these kinds of numbers, especially since Sabonis went a perfect 5-for-5 from the field.

A team that can't score AND is a traffic cone on the other end? The Kings are going to be a tough watch this season.

San Antonio Spurs: The League Has Figured Victor Wembanyama Out

As the San Antonio Spurs experiment with a three-guard lineup so they don't hurt anyone's feelings, Victor Wembanyama remains the most important part of the franchise's success.

Yes, the Frenchman may be the most impressive defensive force the NBA has ever seen, but is his offense an area of concern? Did the Oklahoma City Thunder show us the blueprint to slowing the 7'4" center down?

Wembanyama went just 1-of-13 from the floor in his season debut, including 0-of-4 from three. The Thunder started their double-big lineup with Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein before unleashing their newest toy, 7'3", 255-pound rookie center Aday Mara.

Throwing as much size and physicality at Wembanyama as possible certainly looked like it worked, as the Thunder remain the greatest threat to the Spurs.

Toronto Raptors: Best Defense in the NBA

The Toronto Raptors are going to be a nightmare to try and score on this season.

With three players (Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles) on B/R's list of the top-30 defenders in the NBA this season, Toronto held the Chicago Bulls to just 92 points on 4-of-36 shooting (11.1 percent) from three in their season opener.

We could also see a balanced offensive attack as Leonard and Barnes battle for alpha status. Four players scored 20 points or more for the Raptors while 12 players in total reached the points column thanks to a blowout win.

The Oklahoma City Thunder have set the standard for defensive excellence in the NBA, although the Raptors may even be better.

Utah Jazz: Still a Year (or Two) Away from Contending

The Utaz Jazz are the sneaky, sexy pick to break out in the West this year, as the franchise is loaded with young talent, some reliable vets and a chest full of draft picks thanks to the Los Angeles Lakers.

As a 20-point loss to the Memphis Grizzlies would indicate, more patience is needed.

No. 2 overall pick Darryn Peterson had just nine points on 3-of-7 shooting in his debut. Ace Bailey is adjusting to a new role off the bench and Jaxson Hayes (minus-27 in his 26 minutes) has big shoes to fill as a starter while Jusuf Nurkić is sidelined with a toe injury.

The Jazz will eventually become a force in the West. It just might take longer than we thought.

Washington Wizards: Anthony Davis is Still HIM

The Washington Wizards shocked everyone when they traded for Anthony Davis at the 2026 deadline despite wallowing at the bottom of the East.

Now finally making his Wizards debut, the 33-year-old, 10-time All-Star showed us why he's still one of the best players in the NBA when healthy and is exactly what this talent-starved Washington team needed.

Davis finished his debut with a game-high 34 points, 12 rebounds, four assists, two steals and a block to lead the Wizards over the Milwaukee Bucks.

articles.title: Villanova Reportedly Set to Exit Philadelphia's Big 5 After Dispute Over New Format
articles.summary: Villanova will be exiting the Big 5 Classic following the 2026-27 season, according to the Philadelphia Inquirer's Jeff Neiburg.
articles.body:
Villanova will be exiting the Big 5 Classic following the 2026-27 season, according to the Philadelphia Inquirer 's Jeff Neiburg .

"While it's possible that a Big 5 Classic remains intact with an annual tripleheader, the current format will be no longer after Villanova was not interested in keeping with the status quo, according to sources," Neiburg reported Thursday. "A different setup that Villanova was into — one that would all but guarantee the Wildcats to not have to play another Big 5 road game — could not be agreed upon by all six schools."

The Big 5 Classic traditionally brings together the biggest basketball schools in Philadelphia: Drexel, La Salle, Penn, Saint Joseph's, Temple, and Villanova.

Neiburg first reported last December that "financial concerns" might reshape the annual event moving forward. For Villanova in particular, there's a question of whether the venture is ultimately worth it.

"When you play 20 conference games, playing an A-10 road game every year is really difficult," coach Kevin Willard said. "You're also taking away a home game when revenue has become extremely important."

Other market factors might be hurting the Big 5 Classic.

Villanova is head and shoulders better than its Philly brethren, and younger fans won't have a recollection of a time when the other five were regularly making the NCAA tournament.

La Salle couldn't even draw a sellout for its matchup with the Wildcats last season, with 2,653 fans on hand for the occasion.

A lot of traditions are falling by the wayside in college basketball and football thanks to conference realignment, scheduling/revenue concerns and an increased emphasis on the postseason.

The Big 5 Classic isn't immune from all of that, and there may come a time when the shared connection between the Philly Big 5 becomes a remnant of the past.

articles.title: NBA season-opening takeaways: Giannis, Lakers, Ant-Melo, Damian Lillard, Tyrese Haliburton and first impressions
articles.summary: Here's what stood out after the NBA's first full slate of games.
articles.body:
Opening Night (part deux) is one of my favorite days of the year. It's a lot of basketball, but you see that's the best part of the experience — it's a lot of basketball.

This is the part where I remind you I used to a be a video coordinator, which can lead to some psychotic tendencies when it comes to watching the sport. I like to have a rotation, games I know I want to watch and flip between those. You can play your way in, you can play your way out. I will absolutely find myself stuck on a game that I just did not see coming.

After absorbing a whole lot of basketball on Wednesday night, my biggest takeaway would be to tap in early this year. Tell a friend to tell a friend. The NBA Cup has generally done a good job of enhancing the underrated competitive aspect of the early season. But watching teams work to forge their identities and find success from Day 1 is very fun to see. Here's what caught my eye:

Giannis debuts in Miami, but Wolves were on the prowl

If you wanted fireworks, you got them in Miami. There was no hesitation from Giannis Antetokounmpo in his Heat debut. He started the game with a midrange pull-up, then unleashed his trademark dynamic and dangerous play in transition. He had zero fear attacking anyone in a blue jersey (including Rudy Gobert): 14 points in 8 minutes in the first quarter, 21 points in the first half. The vibes were high in Miami.

But the vibes were also high for the Timberwolves. This is a unit that refreshed its identity this offseason, and Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball made sure to put a stamp on that in their first game together — a 131-106 victory . The duo combined to make 14 3s, while the Heat made only 8. Edwards had 21 points in the first half and ended with 45 on the night.

LaMelo allows Edwards to play off-ball more, and Edwards being able to fly off a stagger or off-ball screens makes him more sudden in the half-court. You know he's going to attack, now you're not always certain where or how. The tricky part is he can and will still take and make the shots that show he does not care about your defender or your scheme. And he did that over and over and over again in this one. When that blend hits, it's tough to deal with.

Ball's playmaking and passing were expected to elevate the Wolves' offensive attack. His shot-making, though, adds another layer on top of that. He can attack early, he can attack often, he can attack when things break down. Combine that with continued room for Ayo Dosunmu and Jaden McDaniels to stay aggressive and Jonathan Kuminga fitting in on both ends, and the Wolves appear ready to hit the ground running. The defensive effort, while not perfect, had a lot of activity, which is encouraging. They will need that base to unlock their offensive attack.

For Miami, it's a reminder that the Heat will have to continue to build throughout the year. They attempted multiple things defensively which will pay off down the line. They will just have to navigate different types of matchups and the different challenges that pop up. The blend of Giannis with the Heat's concepts looked great at times and rough at others. These are the moments you work through.

The Lakers no longer have the services of LeBron James and immediately pivoted to shift the roster around Luka Dončić. There was a feeling throughout training camp and preseason that JJ Redick had a belief in this team, having a different type of depth that could unlock a different version of the Lakers. Stephen Curry did not feel the same way, scoring 16 of the Warriors' first 21 points against the Lakers on Wednesday. The trouble for the Warriors was they scored just 19 points in the second quarter, and 16 points in the third quarter, with the Lakers breezing to a 127-105 win .

The battle for the Lakers going forward is finding the right blend of offense and enough defense to sustain it. Luka Dončić is, was and will be Luka Dončić. Austin Reaves continues to feel unlocked within this context. Walker Kessler, quite literally did not miss a shot (12 for 12 from the floor) in his Laker debut. When all three of your new big three can put up 20, you can go home feeling good about the job you've done.

And for Kessler, when you put yourself in the company of Wilt Chamberlain (14 for 14 for the Lakers in March 1969; most shots without a miss in Lakers history, Kessler is now No. 2), you've done a great job. More important, though, was his work on the defensive end. His timing on his rotations and his ability to roam and protect the paint add a layer to the activity the Lakers want to provide on that end of the floor. The Lakers' ability to get stops also unlocks Kessler's ability to rim run in transition. As much as we want to tap the pick-and-roll button with Kessler, he's shown a knack for cutting and flashing into open areas at the right time. The Lakers will have to continue to work to have this kind of success, but it's key to get early success to further buy-in.

As far as Golden State goes, can someone please give Stephen Curry some help? Please.

The Klaw returns to Toronto (and the Bulls could not escape)

You could feel something special in the air as Kawhi Leonard made his official return to Toronto . As the Raptors introduced the roster, Kawhi came out and did the Klaw hand motion like he was the Texas Tornado. Then he hit an early 3, and it was very clear the Raptors were here to make sure the Bulls did not have a good time.

For Toronto to get 20-plus points each out of Kawhi, Scottie Barnes, RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley speaks to its future offensive synergy. But the real key was its defense. I cannot think of a worse team to face as you are working to build your identity than the Raptors. Size, length, activity, ball pressure, rotations. The Bulls had 27 made field goals; they also had 27 turnovers. If you're not ready to execute against the Raptors, prepare for a series of precarious moments.

Damian Lillard, Portland enjoy basketball again

There was the moment in the Moda Center that everyone had anticipated for months. It was Damian Lillard's return home, but it was Blazers PA announcer Mark Mason letting the world know he was "wearing the letter O" that sealed it. For the city of Portland, amid a sea of chatter that should never exist, the focus was finally on the court.

Wednesday night not only marked the return of Lillard but the debut of Ja Morant. It was Ja who hit a pull-up 3, and it was the Blazers who jumped out to a 21-0 run in this one. By the time you got to the Dame sequence of hitting a 3, rolling into a stepback from the logo, the crowd was ready and reminding the world basketball belonged in the city of Portland.

To the game, questions may abound about the guards the Blazers have and how it all fits. Many of the questions will be fair, but there is plenty of room for all of them to contribute and grow. Dame has room to be Dame without being overtasked. His off-ball movement and gravity will lift the team. For all of the talk about Morant, he appeared to play with a certain level of joy. Within the first six minutes of action, he hit a pull-up 3, contested a layup on a fastbreak, got into it with Devin Booker, dove on the floor to knock a ball off Collin Gillespie and forced a turnover. I don't know if buy-in will be the full issue here.

I'm uncertain of what the Blazers will accomplish in this tough Western Conference, but their fight and belief shouldn't be ignored. Lillard and Morant both have a chance to rewrite their stories. Do you think they are unaware? Do you think Jrue Holiday will ever take a day off? Do you think Scoot Henderson is worse for wear for being able to learn and play along those three? Do you think Robert Williams III is not happy to have a certain level of health? Do you think Micah Nori worked this hard for this long in this league to go backward? Adversity may knock on the door, but that shouldn't ignore the ceiling — the ceiling for a team that has no business playing anywhere else than Portland, Oregon.

We've known Tyrese Haliburton would be returning, and we've known what that would mean for the Indiana Pacers. He got the moment to prove it without a shadow of a doubt: a fourth quarter where he shot 4 of 4 from the field, 5 of 5 from the line and scored 13 points to help the Pacers win on the road in New Orleans in his first game since he tore his Achilles during the 2025 NBA Finals. He delivered a reminder of how much he raises the Pacers' ceiling, and how they have the ability to shape-shift, compete and attack to find a way to win.

It's easy to forget how important that was to their formula to get to the Finals. Watching Haliburton and Pascal Siakam execute time and time again in the fourth was a clear statement: We're not a fun team to deal with. And Ivica Zubac continues to have an undercurrent impact for this team with his defensive nuance and offensive ceiling.

I would be remiss if I did not give a salute to the Pelicans for their efforts. I believed in the talent of the roster, I believed in the coach, I wondered how the pieces would come together. This regular-season debut felt different. There was a compete level that could work to get the most out of this group. There was a Haliburton/Zubac pick-and-roll where Zion Williamson's man was on the wing. Not only was Zion showing early help from the weakside, he stole the pocket pass to Zubac and the Pelicans scored on the other end. If they are going to compete defensively and complement each other offensively, this will be an annoying team to deal with.

• Is everyone sure they know how good the Houston Rockets are? Like, imagine the defense stays at the same level but they play with more force and movement offensively. Imagine that the stops they generate actually turn into points on the other end. Imagine the reps that Jabari Smith Jr., Amen Thompson and Co. took last year set them up for success this year.

Two possessions in their 128-110 win over the Mavs. stood out to me. The first: the Rockets were up 14 in the second quarter, Kevin Durant gets the ball, and it looks like an iso. Alperen Şengün flashes from the block to the elbow and looks like he's going to set a flare for Marcus Smart, but he slips, Smart slides to the wing, and KD hits him for a 3. The second: Şengün got a double team late in the second quarter, dribbled out of the post to the 3-point line, saw the double leave, and immediately drove left, spun and tried to finish. Little wrinkles mindset-wise can elevate Houston.

• Orlando vs. Atlanta was secretly my favorite matchup of the night. The Magic were working to find ways to get to tempo and ball movement in the half-court, while the Hawks were working to find help and rotate on defense. Atlanta was trying to execute in the half-court, while Orlando was trying to return to form in the half-court defensively.

Both teams played with belief. Paolo Banchero and Jalen Johnson played with a high level of confidence and comfort. Orlando wanted to get to a lot of inverted pick-and-roll, and Atlanta was able to seal the game with Nickeil Alexander-Walker screening for Johnson. You should lock in on the Eastern Conference because the Magic jumped out of the gates and Atlanta responded with an early 29-9 run.

• I've said Ty Jerome's game is decel and shoot stepbacks, what do you mean he did that to the tune of 45 points ? Between that and the Cam Boozer fastbreak where he politely asked Jaren Jackson Jr. to move out of the way, it was a fun night for Memphis.

• I think the Washington Wizards are really fun. It was very funny to see Trae Young trade the preseason "I will get downhill and pass to anyone" for "I do remember exactly how I can draw fouls, so you know." Young and Anthony Davis dropped reminders of how good they are with a roster of youth ready to compete. Kyshawn George probably should have made my breakout players if he's going to drive to the basket like Mark Henry or Derrick Henry.

• The Brooklyn Nets' ABA throwback uniforms and court are phenomenal, and I think Julius Randle is going to have an outstanding year for them.

articles.title: LaMelo Ball Responds to Lonzo Calling Him Out For Missed Traveling Call in Viral Video, 'He Hatin'
articles.summary: Minnesota Timberwolves star point guard LaMelo Ball brushed off his brother, Lonzo, for calling out his missed traveling violation in a viral video.
articles.body:
Minnesota Timberwolves star point guard LaMelo Ball brushed off his brother, Lonzo, for calling out his missed traveling violation in a viral video.

Ball's step-back three-pointer during his team debut with the Timberwolves quickly drew attention online and even got called out by the ESPN broadcast desk for being a travel:

The elder Ball couldn't help but find the humor in the viral video, and he admitted it was a travel in his post on social media:

However, the 25-year-old wasn't having any of it, telling ESPN's Michael Eaves and Nicole Briscoe on SportsCenter , "He hatin'. He hatin'. See, I gotta give him a call right now, 'cause with the family, he know what you supposed to do. Even if I'm wrong, I'm right. That's how it go, I gotta teach that boy."

Ball finished with 21 points and six assists in his Timberwolves debut to help lead his team to a 131-106 victory on the road.

Ball and the Timberwolves will return to action on Friday against the Orlando Magic, and he should be careful with the extra steps he takes before his shots.

articles.title: Chad Johnson Responds to Anthony Edwards' Trash Talk After Viral Videos From Wolves-Heat
articles.summary: Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards and longtime former NFL wide receiver Chad Johnson exchanged some words during Minnesota's season-opening, 131-106 road win over the Miami Heat on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards and longtime former NFL wide receiver Chad Johnson exchanged some words during Minnesota's season-opening, 131-106 road win over the Miami Heat on Wednesday night.

Johnson was in attendance for Wednesday's game, and Edwards was well aware of it, as multiple videos of them jawing with each other went viral on social media:

Ochocinco offered a humorous response to the drama in a post on X:

The beef between Johnson and Edwards began last week when Ochocinco challenged some comments made by Ant.

Per Caroline John of Yahoo Sports, Edwards spoke about his expectations for the T-Wolves during a live stream, saying, "We gon' foul the s--t out you. It's a bunch of bulls--t this year."

On a subsequent episode of Nightcap (h/t John), Johnson questioned whether Edwards and the T-Wolves would truly be a factor during the 2026-27 NBA campaign:

"Hey, that little soliloquy he gave. I mean, it was fine and dandy," Johnson said. "You know, they could be on the BS or whatever they talking about. I know they exciting. They'll be fun to watch, but they ain't scary. They going to be entertaining. You know, it's going to be worth the money. You know, outside of that, I mean, they ain't they ain't really scaring nobody."

Johnson followed that up by suggesting that the Heat were going to beat the Timberwolves in the first game of the season.

Instead, Minnesota dominated from start to finish, and Edwards looked to be the best player on the court, finishing with a game-high 45 points.

articles.title: Clippers dedicate opening-night win to suspended owner Steve Ballmer: 'We're still fighting for him'
articles.summary: Steve Ballmer was at the game "in spirit," according to Darius Garland.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Clippers took the court at Intuit Dome on Wednesday without one of their biggest fans cheering them on. That would be team owner Steve Ballmer, who is suspended for the entire season over violating NBA salary cap rules.

Ballmer may not have been able to attend the contest — which the Clippers won 121-96 over the Sacramento Kings — in person, but he was there in spirit. After the game, Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue opened his presser by dedicating the win to Ballmer .

"First off, that win was for Mr. Ballmer," Lue said. "Just want to say thank you for everything and we're still fighting for him."

Ballmer was suspended as part of the NBA investigation into the Kawhi Leonard signing. The team and owner were accused of paying Leonard additional funds through "no-show jobs" as a way to circumvent the NBA salary cap.

The league launched an investigation into the situation after journalist Pablo Torre unveiled the plot on his podcast. After months of investigating, the NBA came down hard on Ballmer and the Clippers , docking the team five future first-round draft picks, fining Ballmer $30 million and suspending him for a year. As part of his suspension, Ballmer is banned "from all league and team activities for one year."

Lue wasn't the only member of the Clippers to pay tribute to Ballmer after the win. Darius Garland, who led the Clippers with 30 points, said Ballmer was " definitely here in spirit ."

After an eventful offseason, one in which the team traded Leonard away , the Clippers face low expectations this season. If Wednesday is any indication, though, the team will use the Ballmer situation as a motivating tactic all year.

Because of that, it's unlikely that narrative will go away anytime soon. If the Clippers can exceed expectations and make a run, you can bet Ballmer's name will continue to be invoked all season.

articles.title: LaMelo Ball gets away with egregious travel during Timberwolves season opener, immediately trash-talks fans
articles.summary: LaMelo Ball took four full steps without dribbling before draining a three-pointer, and the video of the blatant no-call has NBA fans stunned.
articles.body: If NBA referees called every travel they saw, games would never end, but blowing the whistle every now and again to remind players that they can't take an infinite number of steps would be appreciated by all involved. Unfortunately, the exact opposite precedent was set during the season opener between the Minnesota Timberwolves and Miami Heat on Wednesday. LaMelo Ball put on an impressive performance in his official debut for Minnesota, scoring 21 points and dishing out six assists in his team's 131-106 victory on the road, but three of his 21 points should not have counted. Just over three minutes into the first quarter, Ball dribbled around a well-set screen that got his defender off balance. Instead of driving towards the basket, he opted to pick his spot beyond the three-point line, but forgot to put the ball on the floor on his way there. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Ball appeared to take every bit of four full steps without taking a dribble. The carry was so egregious that each of the announcers on the broadcast couldn't help but call out how bad the no-call was. The 25-year-old guard immediately talking trash to some courtside fans after he made the three made the whole scene that much worse. Then again, Ball and essentially every other player in the league have gotten away with traveling with the basketball throughout their NBA careers. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW-UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Oftentimes, the missed travel calls take place with players driving to the basket and getting away with an extra half-step while carrying the basketball. For Ball not to get whistled while standing well beyond the three-point line is a bit of a surprise, even by NBA standards. As for the contest itself, the Timberwolves looked as good and entertaining as expected with their new two-headed monster of Anthony Edwards and Ball in the 25-point win over Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Heat. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Edwards finished the night with 45 points, including nine made three-pointers, to go along with 10 rebounds. While the duo of Ball and Edwards combining for 66 points stands out, maybe the most promising stat line to look at if you're a Minnesota fan is that the two only turned the ball over five times total in the win.

articles.title: Knicks Fans Go Viral After Naming Newborn Son Knickson Fyve In Honor of Team's Historic NBA Title
articles.summary: Sports fans naming their children after players on championship-winning teams is nothing new, which means plenty of New York Knicks fans likely considered Jalen after Jalen Brunson or even Karl after Karl-Anthony Towns after the team won the 2026 NBA Finals.
articles.body:
Sports fans naming their children after players on championship-winning teams is nothing new, which means plenty of New York Knicks fans likely considered Jalen after Jalen Brunson or even Karl after Karl-Anthony Towns after the team won the 2026 NBA Finals.

But one family put its own twist on things.

WABC-TV reported one family named their newborn son Knickson Fyve following New York's championship run:

The new name phonetically sounds like "Knicks in five," which is exactly how many games it took Brunson and Co. to defeat the San Antonio Spurs in the Finals.

And now this family will always remember exactly that.

articles.title: NBA Refs Call Out LaMelo Ball's Travel After Viral Video From T-Wolves' Opener vs. Heat
articles.summary: Most fans watching Wednesday's game between the Minnesota Timberwolves and Miami Heat knew LaMelo Ball got away with a travel.
articles.body:
Most fans watching Wednesday's game between the Minnesota Timberwolves and Miami Heat knew LaMelo Ball got away with a travel.

The official social media account of the NBA Referees responded to the play Thursday and said, "For everyone asking, 'how is this legal?' It's not! He gathers with his right foot on the floor and would be permitted two steps by rule (left-right). He takes four steps after gathering the ball and travels."

Video of the play went viral Tuesday and even drew an amused response from Ball's brother, Lonzo:

When told of Lonzo's post during an interview with SportsCenter after the game, LaMelo said , "He hatin'. He hatin'. See, I gotta give him a call right now, 'cause with the family, he know what you supposed to do. Even if I'm wrong, I'm right. That's how it go, I gotta teach that boy."

Missed travel or not, Ball's debut with the Timberwolves went well.

He finished with 21 points, six assists, two steals and two rebounds and helped lead his new team to a dominant 131-106 victory over Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Heat. Ball was excellent, but he was also a secondary option for the visitors with Anthony Edwards stealing the show.

Edwards dropped 45 points and 10 rebounds in just 33 minutes in a good sign of what is to come for the Timberwolves' new backcourt duo.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard Says 'You Can't Rush Greatness' After Playing 24 Minutes in Return to Raptors
articles.summary: Kawhi Leonard doesn't seem concerned about when he will be able to ramp up to full participation after seeing limited playing time in his Wednesday night return to the Toronto Raptors.
articles.body:
Kawhi Leonard doesn't seem concerned about when he will be able to ramp up to full participation after seeing limited playing time in his Wednesday night return to the Toronto Raptors.

Leonard, whose reunion with Toronto was delayed until his trade from the Los Angeles Clippers was finalized a month ago, scored 23 points in just 24 minutes of a 135-92 season-opening win over the Chicago Bulls.

"I don't put targets. You can't rush greatness," Leonard said when asked Wednesday night about a target date for when he'll play a full allotment of minutes.

Leonard continued: "Whenever the medical thinks I could push forward, and I'm feeling great— whatever numbers we're looking at, or they're looking at, then that's when that time will come.

"I'm just happy to be out there and try to do the best I can with my minutes."

Leonard shot just 5-for-17 from the field and 2-for-6 from deep Wednesday night, but was perfect on 11 attempts from the foul line against the Bulls.

He also added six rebounds, two assists, four steals and a block in his first game with the Raptors since leading the team to a title in 2019.

Raptors coach Darko Rajaković said after the game he isn't worried about Leonard's relative shooting inefficiency.

"I thought the shots that he was getting were really good shots. He's still building his capacity to play... every minute that he spends on the court, that capacity is going to just go up," Rajaković said.

Rajaković also said Leonard had asked him for more playing time after he was subbed out late in the blowout.

About his successful request for more playing time in the fourth quarter, Leonard said, "I haven't gotten a chance to play a lot in training camp, so any minutes I can get, or continue to play— I know we was blowing them out, but the goal was to try to get 23, 24 minutes tonight, and I just need more reps to learn plays."

Leonard continued, "You get better on the floor, and trying things, and shooting the ball when you're open. You can't wait 'til practice and just shoot 100 shots. You need game reps."

The Raptors initially agreed to acquire Leonard from the Clippers in June. The trade was finalized in late September following an NBA investigation into alleged salary cap circumvention.

Rajaković told reporters last month the Raptors planned to keep age and injury history in mind while ramping up Leonard, who said last month he was "wasn't able to really do much with the trade in a holding pattern."

Leonard will get his next opportunity to continue re-adjusting to the Raptors after seven years away when his team hits the road for a Friday night matchup against Anthony Davis and the Washington Wizards, who opened their season Wednesday night with a win over the Milwaukee Bucks.

articles.title: JuJu Watkins, Sarah Strong Headline 2026 Women's AP Preseason All-America Team
articles.summary: Members of the women's college basketball media are expecting a return to form from USC star JuJu Watkins.
articles.body:
Members of the women's college basketball media are expecting a return to form from USC star JuJu Watkins.

Watkins, who missed all of 2025-26 due to a torn ACL, was one of five players selected for the Associated Press' preseason All-America team . UConn's Sarah Strong, the reigning national player of the year, was a near-consensus pick with 30 out of 31 votes.

Speaking about Strong, UConn coach Geno Auriemma told the AP's Doug Feinberg that "it's pretty hard to get that much better" than she was as a sophomore.

"But it's not that hard to get better at some things that she wants to get better at," he said. "And I think what we'll see is a much more aggressive Sarah, much more intentional, much more understanding."

Strong could still collect all of the major individual honors if she just repeats her production (18.4 PTS, 7.7 REB, 3.8 AST, 3.4 STL) from a season ago.

With Watkins, the questions go beyond what kind of player she is post-ACL tear. Her absence allowed Jazzy Davidson to run the show in Los Angeles. The true freshman was USC's leader in points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks.

Between Watkins and Davidson, the Trojans boast the most electric backcourt in the country. However, the pair could wind up splitting votes between each other when it comes to postseason awards and accolades.

Partially because of that, Notre Dame guard Hannah Hidalgo might be the toughest challenger in Strong's repeat bid to be the national player of the year.

The junior led Division I in steals (5.6) for the second time and was top scorer in the ACC (25.3).

"I don't focus on the numbers ever," she told Feinberg. "All the numbers I put up last year was never about me saying, 'OK, I'm going to get this amount of points and this amount of steals.' I go out every single game and play every game like it's my last, and the numbers just come with how I play."

Even with the addition of Princeton guard Madison St. Rose, Hidalgo is going to shoulder a sizable offensive load for Notre Dame. Add that to her elite perimeter defending and it could tip the scales in her favor when voters weigh in at the end of the season.

articles.title: Nikola Jokic chasing NBA history in Nuggets season opener
articles.summary: Jokic eyes NBA history as Denver opens its season against Oklahoma City.
articles.body:
The NBA season gets underway for the Denver Nuggets on Thursday, with superstar center Nikola Jokic looking to make history in the team's opening-night matchup against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Jokic enters the 2026-27 campaign tied with basketball legend Oscar Robertson for the most triple-doubles recorded by a player in a season opener, with both stars achieving the feat four times. Another triple-double against the Thunder would give Jokic sole possession of the NBA record.

The three-time NBA Most Valuable Player has established himself as one of the league's most versatile players, consistently contributing as a scorer, rebounder and playmaker. Now, he has an opportunity to add another milestone to his already impressive career.

Jokic looks to extend season-opening record

Jokic recorded his fourth season-opening triple-double last year, finishing with 21 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists against the Golden State Warriors.

Despite his outstanding individual performance, Denver fell 137-131 in overtime, leaving the Nuggets eager to begin the new season with a better result.

The Serbian center continued to deliver elite production throughout the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 27.7 points, 12.9 rebounds and 10.7 assists per game. His all-around performances helped guide Denver into the playoffs, although the Nuggets ultimately suffered a first-round elimination at the hands of the Minnesota Timberwolves.

With another season ahead, Jokic will once again be central to Denver's hopes of competing for a championship. His ability to influence games in multiple ways makes him one of the NBA's most difficult players to defend.

Denver's season opener presents a challenging matchup against Oklahoma City, as the Nuggets begin their 2026-27 regular season on the road.

Jokic and the Nuggets know what it takes to reach the top of the league, having captured the NBA championship in 2023. Jokic was named Finals MVP following that title-winning run, further cementing his status among the game's elite.

The Nuggets will hope to build on their previous success and make another deep postseason run this year.

However, Thursday's contest offers Jokic an immediate individual milestone to pursue. If he records another triple-double, he will move ahead of Robertson and become the NBA's outright leader for season-opening triple-doubles.

With history within reach, all eyes will be on Jokic as Denver opens its campaign against Oklahoma City.

images.caption: Oct 11, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Chicago Bulls forward Leonard Miller (11) defends on Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic (15) in the second quarter at Ball Arena. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images

Apr 30, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic (15) shoots the ball over Minnesota Timberwolves center Rudy Gobert (27) in the second half during game six of the first round of the 2026 NBA Playoffs at Target Center. Mandatory Credit: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images

articles.title: LeBron James gets unique jersey patch for record-breaking 24th NBA season
articles.summary: LeBron James is marking his record-breaking 24th NBA season with a special jersey patch celebrating his unprecedented longevity. The Philadelphia 76ers star...
articles.body:
LeBron James has another piece of NBA history attached to his uniform. The Philadelphia 76ers star will wear a special commemorative jersey patch throughout his record-breaking 24th NBA season, celebrating a career that has continued to produce milestones well into his 40s.

The NBA and Topps announced the patch on Oct. 20, giving James a distinctive way to mark his unprecedented longevity. The patches will be removed from his jersey after each game, with select examples destined for rare trading cards that preserve a physical piece of his historic season.

The recognition arrives as James begins a new chapter in Philadelphia after leaving the Los Angeles Lakers. At 41, he is still competing at basketball's highest level, and his latest milestone highlights both his remarkable durability and his continued place among the league's most recognizable stars.

The special patch celebrates James' 24th NBA season

The commemorative patch features the number 24 beneath an "NBA Seasons" banner, alongside a silhouette of James performing his signature pregame chalk toss. Its design connects the achievement directly to one of basketball's most recognizable players.

James became the first player in NBA history to reach 24 seasons when the 2026-27 campaign began. The achievement extends the longevity record he established during his previous season with the Lakers, moving him beyond the career length of every other NBA player.

Rather than celebrating a single game or championship, the patch recognizes an entire career milestone. It will accompany James throughout the season, turning his regular-season appearances into additional reminders of how unusually long he has remained an active NBA star.

Topps plans to turn game-worn patches into rare cards

The patch announcement also introduces a collectible element. The patches will be removed from James' jersey after each game, with select examples incorporated into exclusive Topps trading cards tied to his record-setting season.

Some of those cards will be designated one-of-one collectibles, meaning only one copy of each specific card exists. The concept gives collectors the opportunity to own memorabilia from a single game during James' unprecedented 24th season.

Topps has not publicly established a complete release schedule for every patch-based card. However, the arrangement links an on-court achievement with the sports memorabilia market, where authenticated items associated with major milestones can attract considerable attention from dedicated collectors.

James begins a new chapter with Philadelphia

The special patch also arrives during a major transition. James left the Lakers after 8 seasons and joined the 76ers, bringing his historic career to Philadelphia as the franchise pursues another championship. His move ended a significant chapter in Los Angeles.

James made his regular-season debut for Philadelphia against the New York Knicks on Oct. 20. The 76ers won 106-100, spoiling the defending champions' celebration at Madison Square Garden while beginning their own campaign with an important road victory.

James contributed 14 points, 9 rebounds, and 7 assists in the win. His performance demonstrated that the veteran remains capable of contributing across multiple areas, although a single game cannot establish how consistently he will produce throughout the demanding regular season.

James' longevity remains unmatched in NBA history

James entered the league in 2003 with the Cleveland Cavaliers and has since played for Cleveland, the Miami Heat, the Lakers, and now the Philadelphia 76ers. His career has spanned multiple generations of NBA players, coaching styles, and changes in how teams approach offense.

His 24th season extends a record that already separated him from other long-serving veterans. Vince Carter previously held the distinction of playing 22 NBA seasons, while James surpassed that mark by continuing his career into a 23rd season with Los Angeles.

James' achievement is especially notable because longevity alone does not explain his continued relevance. He has remained a productive player while carrying substantial responsibilities, and his career totals include the NBA's all-time scoring record. Maintaining that level of production over 2 decades is exceptionally rare.

The patch adds another collectible to James' legacy

Game-worn memorabilia can connect fans to specific moments in sports history. In James' case, the patches offer a direct link to individual appearances during a season that already stands apart because of its record-setting length.

The one-of-one format also gives certain cards a unique identity. A patch taken from a particular game cannot be identical in provenance to one removed from another appearance, making each authenticated piece potentially interesting to collectors who follow James' career closely.

While the commemorative patch celebrates James' remarkable longevity, his transition to Philadelphia brings a different set of challenges as he adjusts to a new team and fresh expectations.

Philadelphia has championship ambitions beyond the celebration

The 76ers did not bring James to Philadelphia to celebrate his longevity. The franchise is looking to compete for a championship, and his experience offers another dimension to a roster featuring established stars and younger talent.

James joins a group that includes Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey, giving Philadelphia another experienced playmaker who can help organize the offense. His ability to create opportunities for teammates could prove particularly useful as the team works to develop chemistry over a long season.

The opening-night victory offered an encouraging start, but the larger test will be consistency, health, and performance against the league's strongest opponents. James' patch marks an individual milestone, while the team's success will ultimately depend on how effectively its players work together.

The Lakers era is over, but James' story continues

James' departure closes an important chapter in Los Angeles. He helped the Lakers win the 2020 NBA championship and delivered years of high-profile performances, leaving behind a franchise legacy that extended beyond individual statistics.

His new uniform represents a different challenge. Philadelphia offers James an opportunity to pursue another championship while extending a career that has already included titles with the Miami Heat, Cleveland Cavaliers, and Lakers.

The 24th-season patch ties these chapters together by focusing on the accomplishment that transcends any single franchise. Whether James adds another championship or more statistical records, his continued presence in the NBA has already secured an unusual place in basketball history.

Fun fact: LeBron James and his son, Bronny James, became the first father-son duo to play together in an NBA regular-season game on Oct. 22, 2024, when they took the court for the Los Angeles Lakers against the Minnesota Timberwolves.

LeBron James will wear a special patch celebrating his record-breaking 24th NBA season with the Philadelphia 76ers.

The design features the number 24, an "NBA Seasons" banner, and a silhouette of his signature chalk toss.

The patches will be removed after games, with select examples appearing in one-of-one Topps trading cards.

The milestone extends James' NBA longevity record as he pursues another championship with his new team.

articles.title: Anthony Edwards Calls Out Heat Reserve for 'Talking Pretty Crazy' During T-Wolves' Blowout Win
articles.summary: Not that Anthony Edwards needs additional motivation to play basketball, but a Miami Heat player may have pushed the Minnesota Timberwolves star to go even further in his 45-point outing in a 131-106 win on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
Not that Anthony Edwards needs additional motivation to play basketball, but a Miami Heat player may have pushed the Minnesota Timberwolves star to go even further in his 45-point outing in a 131-106 win on Wednesday night.

Speaking to reporters after Minnesota's victory, Edwards called out a Heat bench player for "talking pretty crazy" at one point during the game.

"A player on their bench was talking trash in one of the dead-ball situations," Edwards said. "I think it kind of crunk me up. He was talking pretty crazy."

Edwards couldn't identify the player from where he was at, but indications are it was Myron Gardner. The Heat, according to the Miami Herald 's Anthony Chiang, did not make Gardner available to the media after practice on Thursday.

Edwards added things got quiet on the Miami bench after he started engaging with them.

"When I start talking to him, he didn't really have too much more to say. I don't really like that," he said. "If you gonna talk s--t, keep talking s--t. Don't get quiet. I think that was pretty much the reason why I was super intense tonight."

Gardner is in his second season with the Heat. He was undrafted out of Little Rock in 2023 and spent two seasons in the G League with the Orlando Magic affiliate in Osceola.

The Heat signed Gardner to their Summer League team in 2025. He signed a standard three-year contract with Miami in February. The 25-year-old played just three minutes on Wednesday night.

If the Heat were trying to get under Edwards' skin, it failed spectacularly. He put up 45 points on 16-of-29 shooting (9-of-17 from three) and grabbed 10 rebounds in just 33 minutes.

Edwards joined Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan as the only players in NBA history to have multiple 40-point games in the season opener for his team. He put up 41 last year in a 118-114 win over the Portland Trail Blazers.

The historic night for Edwards spoiled Giannis Antetokounmpo's Heat debut after being acquired in an offseason trade with the Milwaukee Bucks.
